set.text:
Haru: Our experiment didn't work. The plants in the dark box grew taller than the ones in the sun.
Ms. Cho: That's interesting. Why do you think that happened?
Haru: I don't know. I expected the sunny ones to do better.
Ms. Cho: Look at the data again. What else do you notice about the dark ones?
Haru: They're taller but very pale and thin.
Ms. Cho: Exactly. Plants without light stretch upward searching for it, but they can't make healthy leaves. So your experiment worked after all.
Haru: Because we learned something we didn't expect?
Ms. Cho: Yes. Unexpected results often teach more than the expected ones. Write that in your report.

patches.why: Ms. Cho's line 'How tall are the dark ones compared with their color?' is ungrammatical/nonsensical (height vs color) and not a natural prompt for Haru's answer; replaced.

set.good: The more you practice, the better you become.
bad: The more you practice, the best you become.
The much you practice, the better you become.
The more you practice, the more better you become.

cz.st: The more you practice, the ___ you become.

set.rule: 'the + 비교급, the + 비교급'은 '~할수록 더 ~하다'라는 뜻이에요. 비교급 good → better를 써요.

patches.why: Word-ordering is not unique: 'The better you become, the more you practice' uses the same tokens and is grammatical, so ord:false. Third distractor 'More you practice, the better...' is colloquially acceptable, replaced by clearly wrong 'the more better'.
